title: EdgeMM: Multi-Core CPU with Heterogeneous AI-Extension and Activation-aware Weight Pruning for Multimodal LLMs at Edge
problem: Multimodal LLMs combine compute-intensive modality encoders with memory-bound LLM decoders, presenting distinct performance bottlenecks that homogeneous CPU designs cannot address efficiently.
motivation: Edge deployment of multimodal LLMs requires efficient handling of dual workload characteristics (compute vs memory bound) within power and area constraints.
method: EdgeMM uses multi-core CPU with heterogeneous AI coprocessors: compute-centric systolic arrays for encoders and memory-centric digital compute-in-memory (CIM) for decoders. Dynamic activation-aware weight pruning and bandwidth management optimize efficiency. Implemented in 22nm commercial technology.
key_novelty: Heterogeneous CPU with dual coprocessor types (systolic + CIM) matched to encoder/decoder workload characteristics.
contributions: 2.84x performance speedup vs laptop RTX 3060 GPU
Heterogeneous systolic-array and CIM coprocessor design
Dynamic activation-aware weight pruning for bandwidth efficiency
limitations: Comparison limited to single GPU baseline; does not discuss power/energy efficiency or area overhead.
primary_theme: Heterogeneous CPU for multimodal LLM edge inference
